questions.question: In Mustasna Mufarragh, how does the noun after إلا take its i'rab?
options: It takes Nasb in all cases
It is Mabnī ʿalā al-fatḥ like the ism of لا نافية للجنس
It takes its i'rab from the Amil — as if إلا were not there
It takes Jarr because إلا functions like a preposition
questions.explanation: When the Mustasna Minhu is absent (Mufarragh), إلا has no independent i'rab effect; the noun's grammatical role is determined entirely by the Amil in the sentence.

questions.question: What case does the Mustasna take after غير or سِوى?
options: Mabnī ʿalā al-fatḥ
Marfūʿ
Majrūr
Mansūb
questions.explanation: غير and سِوى are themselves particles that govern Jarr, so the Mustasna following them is always Majrūr; غير itself then takes the case the Mustasna would have taken with إلا.

questions.question: In which situation does لا نافية للجنس lose its amal?
options: When its ism is shibh muḍāf
When its ism is nakirah mufrad
When a maʿrifa follows it
When the khabar is mentioned before the ism
questions.explanation: لا نافية للجنس requires a nakirah ism; if a maʿrifa follows, the amal is void and repetition of لا becomes obligatory. The same applies when a fāṣil intervenes between لا and its ism.

questions.question: The term مُفَرَّغ in Mustasna grammar refers to:
options: An exception whose i'rab is fixed as Nasb regardless of context
An exception in which the Mustasna is Majrūr after a particle
An exception in which the Mustasna Minhu is absent
An exception that follows a definite noun
questions.explanation: مُفَرَّغ means 'empty' — the sentence is 'emptied' of the Mustasna Minhu, leaving the excepted noun to fill the grammatical role directly.

questions.question: What is إن زائدة?
options: A pleonastic إن that adds no meaning — its presence voids the amal of Hijazi مَا
An إن that adds emphasis by linking two clauses
An إن that makes both sides of a sentence Majzūm
An إن that converts a nominal sentence into a conditional
questions.explanation: إن زائدة is purely expletive — it carries no semantic weight — and its insertion after Hijazi مَا is one of the three conditions that nullify مَا's amal, returning both ism and khabar to Rafʿ.

questions.question: What was the primary reason Bani Isra'eel rejected Prophet Muhammad ﷺ despite recognizing him from the Torah?
options: They were driven by حَسَد — unwilling to accept prophethood going to another nation
They doubted the authenticity of the Quranic revelation
They believed prophethood had ended permanently with Musa ﷺ
They claimed the Torah's description matched a future prophet, not Muhammad ﷺ
questions.explanation: Bani Isra'eel had already recognized the Prophet ﷺ from the Torah's descriptions; their rejection stemmed from حَسَد — resentment that prophethood was given to a nation other than their own.

questions.question: What is the Quranic verdict on Sulaiman ﷺ and magic?
options: Sulaiman ﷺ learned magic but employed it only for righteous purposes
Sulaiman ﷺ was given knowledge of sihr as one of his divine miracles
Sulaiman ﷺ forbade magic but could not prevent the shayateen from spreading it
Sulaiman ﷺ was entirely innocent of magic; it was the shayateen who taught sihr
questions.explanation: The Quran explicitly states مَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ — Sulaiman ﷺ never disbelieved nor practiced magic; his kingdom rested on divine miracles, and the shayateen alone were responsible for teaching sihr.

questions.question: What was the role of Harut and Marut in Babylon?
options: They were sent to punish Bani Isra'eel for the sin of calf worship
They were angels who demonstrated that divine miracles surpass magic
They were sent as a divine فِتْنَة, always warning 'do not disbelieve' before teaching magic
They were tasked with exposing the shayateen who had spread sihr among the people
questions.explanation: Harut and Marut were sent as a test (فِتْنَة) from Allah; before imparting any knowledge they always issued the warning not to disbelieve, making each learner's choice a matter of personal responsibility.

questions.question: Which term means 'coverings or sheaths' — used by Bani Isra'eel to claim their hearts could not receive the Prophet's message?
options: لَعْنَة
حَسَد
فِتْنَة
غُلْف
questions.explanation: غُلْف (plural of أَغْلَف) means coverings or sheaths; Bani Isra'eel used this claim to suggest their hearts were sealed off, but Allah responded by declaring it a consequence of their own disbelief and cursing them.

questions.question: What distinguishes a مُعْجِزَة from سِحْر?
options: A مُعْجِزَة has permanent effects, while the effects of سِحْر always fade with time
A مُعْجِزَة is always visible to everyone, while سِحْر can only be perceived by its victim
A مُعْجِزَة can be learned through prolonged study, while سِحْر requires a pact with shayateen
A مُعْجِزَة is exclusively from Allah and cannot be learned; سِحْر is a human craft bounded by Allah's permission
questions.explanation: A مُعْجِزَة is a divine miracle granted only by Allah and cannot be acquired or replicated; سِحْر is a real but human craft that can only harm with Allah's permission.

questions.question: In Salat al-Khawf, what do soldiers of each group do after the imam gives salam?
options: They defer the remaining raka'at until the threat has passed
They pray their missed raka'at independently
They repeat the entire prayer together as one unit
They join the opposing group to complete the remaining raka'at jointly
questions.explanation: Each group follows the imam for its portion of the prayer; once the imam finishes and gives salam, each group independently completes whatever raka'at they missed while on guard duty.

questions.question: Which item is never omitted from a woman's kafan, even at the absolute minimum (Kafan Kifaya)?
options: The Qamees (shirt)
The Khimar (head covering)
The Izar (lower wrap)
The Lifafa (outer sheet)
questions.explanation: The Khimar is the head covering specific to the woman's kafan; it is retained even when only the bare minimum is used, reflecting the obligation to cover the head that extends even to burial.

questions.question: For how long may Salatul Janazah be performed at the grave if burial occurred without it?
options: Until the following Friday prayer
Three days, as long as the body has not begun to disintegrate
One day only, before the next Fajr prayer
Two days, to allow distant family to attend
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Yusuf's relied-upon position permits Salatul Janazah at the grave for up to three days after burial, provided the body has not yet begun to decompose.

questions.question: What is a لَحْد?
options: A niche cut into the side wall of the grave toward the qibla
The perfumed compound applied to the head and places of sajda after ghusl
Unbaked mud bricks used to seal the grave opening
The outer shroud layer that wraps the entire body
questions.explanation: The لَحْد is the preferred grave type in which a niche is carved into the qibla-facing side wall; the body is laid in this recess, which is then sealed — preferably with لَا بِن (unbaked bricks).

questions.question: What is حَنُوط applied to after the deceased's ghusl?
options: The entire body before the first layer of kafan is wrapped
The outside surface of the completed kafan
The hands and feet only
The head and the places of sajda
questions.explanation: حَنُوط is a perfumed compound applied specifically to the head and the seven places of sajda after ghusl is complete, before the body is wrapped in kafan.
